Subject: Severe drop in throughput during your rolling upgrade (us-west-2)

Hi Rishi —

We observed a sudden collapse in request throughput and a spike in 5xx rates for our checkout flows yesterday during what we believe was one of your rolling upgrade waves in us-west-2. Impact window we see in our telemetry: 2027-04-18 02:13:20Z — 2027-04-18 02:26:05Z (UTC).

Business impact: ~6% of payments timed out / retried, causing checkout failures for about 12 minutes. This maps to a few thousand failed attempts and a measurable revenue hit for the hour.

Can you confirm whether a platform operation coincided with this window, whether this is eligible for an SLO remedy, and what evidence you can provide? We need the verified downtime/throughput-impact window and a plan for next steps (credit calculation + postmortem).

I can share our request_id samples if that helps — attaching a quick CSV excerpt.

Attachments: swiftpay_samples_excerpt.csv (csv)

— Laura

Laura / Rishi —

We pulled the control-plane and per-host metrics for us-west-2. Preliminary findings: there was a rolling upgrade starting at 2027-04-18T02:05:00Z and a shard rebalancing event between 02:12:00Z and 02:28:00Z that coincides with the window you reported. During that interval we see a sustained drop in provisioned concurrency and a burst of preemption/restarts on a subset of serving hosts.

Concrete artifacts attached:
- swiftpay_logs_20270418.zip (contains host-level logs, routing traces, and shard assignment deltas)
- latency_graph_20270418.png (aggregated P50/P90/P99 for the region)

Quick note on quoting: "On Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700 Laura Chen <laura.chen@swiftpay.com> wrote:"

 > We observed a sudden collapse in request throughput...

We will mark the timeframe 2027-04-18T02:13:00Z — 2027-04-18T02:26:00Z as the candidate impact window. We still need to reconcile sampling boundaries and any client-side retries that happened just outside that range.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Rishi / Marissa to confirm if the candidate window meets SLO remediation rules.
2) If eligible, compute proportional credit using the standard SLO formula and propose a remedy.
3) Produce an RCA draft and share within 5 business days; we can accelerate if SwiftPay wants a live triage.

— Karthik

Laura —

Thanks Karthik for the quick analysis. I reviewed the artifacts and verified the candidate window. Our verification summary (draft):

- Verified impact window: 2027-04-18T02:13:20Z — 2027-04-18T02:26:05Z (matches SwiftPay samples and our routing traces).
- Root cause (short summary): simultaneous shard rebalance + an edge autoscaler misconfiguration during a rolling upgrade caused underprovisioning for a subset of hot shards; caused increased queuing and a short period of 5xxs/timeout errors.
- Severity: SLO breach for request availability for that region and period; qualifies for proportional remedy under the SLA.

Provisional compensation calculation (subject to procurement/finance review):
- Covered window duration: ~12 minutes 45 seconds.
- Per contract (section 4.2), proportional credit = (unavailable_seconds / billing_period_seconds) * monthly_fee.
- For a rough initial offer, we estimate the proportional credit to be approximately 0.009% of monthly committed spend for that billing period; we will refine when procurement provides exact billing period baseline.

Requested items to finalize:
1) SwiftPay to confirm baseline monthly committed spend and billing period to compute the exact credit.
2) Procurement contact for issuing the credit (cc'd if different).

RCA timeline and next steps:
- We will produce an internal RCA and a customer-facing blameless postmortem draft by 2027-04-23 (5 business days).
- If you want an earlier sync, we can schedule a 30-minute triage with infra and product tomorrow.

Attachments: swiftpay_logs_20270418.zip, latency_graph_20270418.png (same as Karthik's bundle).

Let me know if the verified window above is acceptable for your credit request — if so we'll prepare a formal credit note and the draft postmortem.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
